title: apaquasi: a Quarto template for good-looking preprints
summary: We released apaquasi, a Quarto template that keeps the machinery of APA formatting but gives preprints and manuscripts a styled, information-rich first page.
content: We write our papers in Quarto, and for APA-style manuscripts the go-to template is the excellent apaquarto by W. Joel Schneider. It handles all the tedious parts (citations, headings, figure and table captions, references) but it produces, by design, a strict APA manuscript. Great for submission, but a bit more formal than it needs to be in (for our own taste).

So we made apaquasi, a quasi-APA fork that keeps all of that machinery but gives the first page a more typeset look: a sidebar with the server, version, peer-review status, licence and keywords, links to the supplementary materials (GitHub, OSF, ...), Open Science badges for open data, materials, code and preregistration, ORCID icons next to author names, a customisable accent colour, optional line numbers, and a two-column body.

Starting a new paper with it is one command, quarto use template DominiqueMakowski/apaquasi, or quarto add DominiqueMakowski/apaquasi for an existing project. It's early days, so feedback and issues are very welcome on the repository!
